audit.whatIsWrong: The two chart layers disagreed: full had rows 4 and 6 on Sylas, content win[] read Zed on all seven. The page rendered two answers to who wins Level 6.
audit.why: Zed is 48.39% over 9093 games — Sylas is ahead on aggregate, and the reason is structural: Hijack (80/55/30) copies Death Mark, and Kingslayer falls to a 6s cooldown with healing that outlasts a burst window. Early is still Zed's: Sylas has to walk into 400 range with Abscond/Abduct while Zed's Q reaches 900.
audit.corrected: Rows 0-3 and 5 to Zed on both layers (content already read Zed, so full side alone); rows 4 and 6 to Sylas on BOTH layers, with whys[4], whys[6] and phases[4].why, phases[6].why rewritten in the same group to match the new verdict.

audit.whatIsWrong: Spike prose was sound but the full-layer ratings sat flat at 5/10 through the levels Zed clearly owns.
audit.why: Zed's spikes are level 3 (E at 5s down to 3s), first item lethality. Sylas's are level 6 Hijack and ranked Kingslayer at 6s.
audit.corrected: Ratings raised to 6/10 through levels 1-5 and dropped to 4/10 on the two Sylas rows.

audit.whatIsWrong: The decisive interaction — Hijack stealing Death Mark, so casting R first hands Sylas the same three-second mark — appeared in spikes/mid prose but never in the trading, cooldown or carry fields where a player looks mid-game. Abscond/Abduct's two-part nature (dash, then a recast that chains him onto you) was never stated either.
audit.why: Riot's E text: he dashes to a location, then may recast to throw chains and pull himself to an enemy he hits. That is two separate commitments, and the punish window is after the second one.
audit.corrected: Stated in breakdown.cooldowns, dosFull[0].d, dosFull[1].d, dontsFull[2].d, enemyWin and breakdown.carry with real numbers: E 13s to 9s, W 12s to 6s, R 80/55/30, Living Shadow 20s.

audit.why: That field exists to carry the real numbers.
audit.corrected: Abscond/Abduct 13s at rank 1 and 9s maxed, Kingslayer 12s to 6s, Hijack 80/55/30.

audit.whatIsWrong: Anti-heal appeared only in a report line and was never tied to a timing.
audit.why: Kingslayer is his sustain and it heals against champions specifically; at rank 5 it is up every 6 seconds.

audit.whatIsWrong: dosFull[1].d was tradeGood verbatim and dontsFull[2].d was tradeBad verbatim, both under unrelated titles (lint COPY_PASTE_BLEED).
audit.why: The heading promised one thing and the body explained another.
audit.corrected: Both replaced with bodies that answer their own titles.

edits.before: Death Mark online — anyone below 60% in lane is now a math problem with a three-second answer.
edits.after: Hijack (80s at rank 1) copies Death Mark — open with R and he answers with your own three-second mark.

edits.before: At 6 you still win by baiting his kit and bursting before he steals your ult.
edits.after: At 6 Hijack turns your own Death Mark back on you — bait it before you commit.

edits.before: Late Zed picks: mark the carry, swap through the peel, and let the death note collect the paperwork.
edits.after: Kingslayer at a 6s cooldown heals him through your combo — pick him from fog or lose the long fight.

edits.before: You out-range and out-pick his engage late with fog Death Marks.
edits.after: Late his Kingslayer healing outlasts your burst in every long fight.

edits.before: - Sylas Abscond / Abduct: matchup-defining — Dash into chain-stun — punish him hard while it is down. Count it out loud if you must. - Your W Living Shadow (swap) has one job: the moment it all goes wrong. - The R has one too: the moment it all goes right.
edits.after: - Abscond / Abduct is 13s at rank 1 and 9s maxed, and it is his only escape — step in the moment he burns it. - Kingslayer drops from 12s to 6s as he ranks it, so keep trades short. - Hijack is 80/55/30: never open with Death Mark.

edits.before: Dash into chain-stun — punish him hard while it is down. Commit on its cooldown, never into it.
edits.after: Abscond dashes 400 and Abduct recasts to chain onto you — trade only once he has spent both halves.

edits.before: W wide, E the slow, Q the scissor from two angles — half a bar of geometry he answered by standing still wrong.
edits.after: Living Shadow is 20s at rank 1 — the swap is your answer to Abduct, so never spend it walking up for a poke.

edits.before: R-ing into a banked stopwatch or held CC — the mark schedules YOUR death three seconds out when the answer was visible.
edits.after: Kingslayer is up every 6s once maxed and heals off you — a long duel refills the bar you just spent energy on.

edits.before: Sylas wins by landing Abscond / Abduct, denying your pattern, and starting the fight your kit wanted ten seconds later.
edits.after: Sylas wins by chaining Abduct onto you, healing the trade back with Kingslayer, and answering your Death Mark with Hijack.

edits.before: Carry through subpoenas — one marked carry per fight; your job is the threshold math and the swap you saved for their answer.
edits.after: Kill Sylas first or not at all — Hijack copies whichever ult decides the fight. If he is already in, swap out and mark the carry behind.

edits.before: Ahead, audit the map: scissor Sylas off every contact, mark the thresholds, and roam the crashes — fed Zed makes health bars legal documents.
edits.after: Ahead, deny the heal: buy Grievous Wounds early, trade only while Kingslayer is down, and roam on crashes before his Hijack matters.

notes: packet.suspectNames flagged 'Death Marks' in spikes[3].text — that is the real ability name pluralised, not a fabrication, so it was left alone. phases[5].rating was already 6/10 and win[5] already 'Zed', so no no-op edits were proposed for that row. The rows 4 and 6 flip to Sylas is the one judgement call here: it is grounded in Hijack copying Death Mark and Kingslayer's 6s ranked cooldown, and it matches the 48.39% win rate, but the packet levelChart reads Zed on all seven rows and therefore disagrees with the flip.
